items.title: Optical Torque Reversal via Electric–Magnetic Spin-Channel Selection
authors: Lv Feng, 侣 冯, Ruohu Zhang, 若虎 张, Zhigang Li, 志刚 李, Bingjue Li, 冰珏 李, Dongdong Lin, 冬冬 林, Binfeng Yun, 斌峰 恽, Guanghao Rui and 光浩 芮
items.summary: Light carrying spin angular momentum (SAM) can exert optical torque and drive particles into rotational motion. Although optical torque reversal has been achieved by tailoring particle properties or incident field parameters, the respective roles of the electric and magnetic components of transverse SAM in governing the torque on an isotropic particle remain unresolved. Here, reversible control of the out-of- plane optical torque on an absorbing isotropic Mie sphere is demonstrated in interference fields formed by two or three plane waves. Two orthogonal linear polarization states selectively activate torque pathways mediated by the electric and magnetic components of the transverse SAM, while intermediate polarization states allow both pathways to coexist. Notably, polarization controls the optical torque by tuning the relative weights of electric and magnetic multipolar contributions. Once higher-order Mie channels become appreciable, competition among these contributions can reverse the total torque and switch the particle rotation between clockwise and counterclockwise directions. These results reveal distinct mechanical roles of the electric and magnetic components of transverse SAM and establish spin-channel selection as a mechanism for polarization-controlled optical torque reversal.

items.title: Hybridization-Induced Enhancement of the Thermoelectric Response in the Kagome Material CsCr6Sb6
authors: Hongye Zhang, Boqin Song, Aifeng Wang, Yisheng Chai, Xiaoyuan Zhou, Ying Zhu, Tianping Ying and Mingquan He
items.summary: Flat bands in kagome lattices provide a prominent route to strongly correlated electronic states. Here we report charge and thermal transport measurements on single crystals of CsCr6Sb6, a kagome Kondo system arising from the hybridization between flat and dispersive bands. The Seebeck coefficient and Nernst signal increase rapidly below TF ~ 70 K, concomitant with the emergence of short-range antiferromagnetic correlations and flat-band resonance. The Nernst coefficient in the intermediate-temperature range of ~30–80 K further follows the universal scaling reported for prototypical heavy-fermion compounds, consistent with the development of strongly renormalized quasiparticles associated with hybridization. Both the Seebeck and Nernst responses reach extrema at a lower temperature Tp ~ 20–25 K, where phonon drag and correlated quasiparticles may both contribute. These results reveal a hybridization-induced enhancement of the thermoelectric response and establish CsCr6Sb6 as a kagome platform for probing flat-band-derived Kondo physics through thermoelectric transport.

items.title: Following Photoexcited Structural Dynamics across Potential Energy Surfaces in Solids
Mineralogical evidence for hydrous carbonaceous chondrite relics in Chang’e-6 regolith
items.summary: Abstract Hydrous carbonaceous chondrites are potential carriers of exogenous water to the Earth–Moon system, yet well-preserved hydrous carbonaceous impactor fragments are rarely found in lunar samples, with previous discoveries limited to the lunar nearside. The Chang’e-6 mission returned the first sample from the farside, providing a unique opportunity to identify the exogenous materials that have added volatiles to this region. We document well‑preserved relics showing C1-like mineralogical features in a Chang’e-6 regolith breccia. They are dominated by fine-grained Mg-rich saponite with partially collapsed basal spacing, along with magnetite, dolomite, sulfides, and organic nanoglobules, matching mineral assemblages of heavily altered carbonaceous chondrites and hydrous materials returned from asteroids Ryugu and Bennu. This diagnostic mineral assemblage and in‑situ space‑weathering overprint confirm that these clasts are surviving fragments of the incoming impactor, and in situ dehydration records water loss during lunar surface exposure. Our study provides the first mineralogical and petrographic evidence for preserved hydrous carbonaceous impact debris in lunar farside regolith, revealing the microscale preservation of hydrated minerals and carbonaceous components and providing new constraints on impact-induced volatile injection and release from carbonaceous materials.

items.title: Tropical forcing and high-latitude ice dynamics: dual engines of millennial climate variability
Canted antiferromagnetism and spin-flop transition in honeycomb $α$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$ revealed by angle-dependent torque magnetometry up to 35 T
items.summary: We report angle-dependent piezocantilever torque measurements on single crystals of the honeycomb magnet $α$-Na$_2$PrO$_3$, proposed to display unconventional magnetism stabilized by anisotropic exchange interactions between spin-orbit entangled, pseudospin 1/2 Pr$^{4+}$ magnetic moments. Previous powder susceptibility observed signatures of a transition at low temperatures to antiferromagnetic order with a weak ferromagnetic moment. From the torque angular dependence in three orthogonal crystallographic planes, we infer a zero-field canted antiferromagnetic structure, with moments almost normal to the honeycomb layers, but weakly canted such as to give rise to a spontaneous magnetization along the in-plane monoclinic $a$-axis, with two magnetic domains related by time reversal. Sharp jumps in the torque angular dependence when the field projection along $a$ changes sign are interpreted as field-induced switching between the two degenerate domains with oppositely aligned ferromagnetic moments. We propose a minimal spin Hamiltonian including easy-axis exchange anisotropy and symmetry-allowed Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) couplings, for which mean-field calculations reproduce the main features of the observed angle-dependent torque. Torque measurements up to 35 T applied almost normal to the layers observe a strong anomaly attributed to proximity to the field-induced spin-flop transition predicted for the above Hamiltonian. We contrast the predicted magnetic phase diagrams for magnetic fields in different orthogonal crystallographic planes normal to the honeycomb layers and discuss how DM interactions convert some transitions into smooth crossovers and stabilize a phase boundary line connecting the spin-flop transition in field normal to the layers to magnetization saturation for in-plane field normal to $a$; such a phase boundary line does not exist in the absence of DM interactions.

items.title: Universal critical behavior in ideal Bose-Einstein condensation
items.summary: The experimental realization of photonic Bose-Einstein condensates has renewed the interest in the critical behavior of the ideal Bose gas, a paradigmatic system generally considered to be well understood. Here we establish a universal thermodynamic classification of ideal Bose-Einstein condensation in terms of experimentally measurable critical observables. We identify three universality classes with distinct critical exponents and singular thermodynamic behavior, arising from the low-energy scaling of the single-particle density of states. Depending on the low-energy scaling exponent of the density of states, which is controlled by dimensionality and confinement, the transition displays either the usual algebraic divergences of thermodynamic susceptibilities, divergent behavior with marginal logarithmic corrections, or a more subtle form of criticality, where only the correlation length diverges. Our work provides a unified framework for equilibrium criticality in noninteracting bosonic systems. This classification applies broadly to atomic, photonic, polaritonic, and magnonic condensates, where dimensionality, confinement, and spectral engineering can strongly reshape the density of states. We connect our thermodynamic classification with previously identified universality classes based on condensate fluctuations and order parameters.

items.title: Resilience of emergent Hamiltonian quantum memories in the presence of noise
items.summary: Emergent Hamiltonians can freeze an entangled state prepared through coherent evolution, since that state is an eigenstate of the Hamiltonian under which it is then stored. We show that the freedom left in this construction allows the storage spectrum to be adapted to a noisy environment without changing the stored state. For a product of Bell pairs prepared from a density wave in an engineered chain, a selection rule prevents local density noise from connecting the target to any of its degenerate partners, so that rescaling the storage Hamiltonian by a factor $α$ moves every transition this noise drives. Under $1/f$ noise, the storage time then grows in proportion to $α$, a result we confirm by evolving the memory under explicit classical $1/f$ fields, whereas for an Ohmic bath the most favorable scale depends on its cutoff. Fermionic loss, treated as a solvable model, includes a transition that rescaling leaves at zero frequency, and an energy shift $μ$ per particle moves it away from zero, with an exact orbital solution giving the resulting lifetimes. Finally, among number-conserving quadratic reference Hamiltonians, $α$ and $μ$ are the only controls that keep the storage Hamiltonian nearest neighbor at every time along the preparation, so that the protocol combines local freezing with control over the storage spectrum.

items.title: Altermagnetic magnon splitting in hematite: from bulk g-wave to planar i-wave
items.summary: Hematite is an insulating iron oxide with both a collinear antiferromagnetic and a weakly ferromagnetic phase with intriguing properties, such as long-range spin transport distances, that make it promising for spintronics applications. It has also been identified as a candidate for g-wave altermagnetism. Here, we present the results of fully relativistic ab initio calculations of the magnon properties of hematite, with a focus on altermagnetic effects. We quantitatively evaluate both the anisotropic and altermagnetic magnon band splitting as well as the magnon lifetimes. We show that dipolar interactions lead to a sizeable non-altermagnetic splitting and a hybridisation between opposite-chirality magnons resulting in a strong reduction of the spin expectation value of magnons close to the Γ point and around nodal planes, even in the collinear out-of-plane phase. Both the frequencies and the lifetimes have a large altermagnetic splitting in the $k_z = 0$ plane, which is characteristic of hematite and not generally expected for g-wave altermagnets. We compare our results to the prototypical, hexagonal g-wave altermagnet manganese telluride, which has four symmetry-protected nodal planes, whereas the fourth nodal surface in hematite is not completely fixed by symmetry. We derive implicit analytical expressions for this surface and discuss how it arises from a combination of rotational and translational symmetry, which leads to a transition to i-wave symmetry at the Brillouin zone boundary. The example of hematite reveals the trigonal altermagnets as a special case where the splitting function exhibits both bulk (g-wave) and planar (i-wave) components, and shows that the point symmetries alone are not sufficient to capture the full symmetry-determined behaviour of the splitting function.

items.title: Drying-induced film formation in redispersible polymer powder: a time-resolved mechanical study
items.summary: The mechanical evolution of latex dispersions during drying remains poorly understood, despite its importance for coatings, adhesives, and construction materials. Here, we use time-resolved mechanical spectroscopy to follow the formation of a polymer film from a dense aqueous latex suspension. The viscoelastic spectra retain a power-law frequency dependence and collapse onto a master curve using time-dependent shift factors, revealing a time-aging superposition principle. Moreover, the frequency shift factor eventually plateaus, suggesting a crossover toward arrested particle dynamics and film formation. This scenario is robustly observed at various temperatures, allowing us to determine an apparent activation energy associated with film formation. Finally, the non-linear response of the dispersion, measured throughout film formation, shows a ductile-to-brittle transition, consistent with the emergence of a solid-like film. Together, these results establish a rheological picture of the transformation from a dense colloidal suspension into a continuous polymer film.

items.title: Molecular engineering for crack-free transfer of single-crystalline oxide membranes onto silicon
items.summary: Heterogeneous integration of single-crystalline complex oxides with silicon offers a route to incorporating their functionalities into next-generation microelectronics. Released from their growth substrates, freestanding oxide membranes enable this integration. However, cracks, wrinkles, and fragmentation during release and transfer limit membrane size and quality. Here, we present an interfacial energy-controlled release strategy that enables crack-free, single-crystalline freestanding oxide membranes with centimeter-scale lateral dimensions. Using SrTiO3 as a model system, time-resolved release studies identify water-induced blistering at the membrane-support interface during prolonged water exposure as the origin of membrane cracking. Lowering the molecular weight of the poly(propylene carbonate) support through polymer deconstruction increases its polarity and surface energy, suppresses interfacial blistering, and reduces organic residue after support removal. The resulting SrTiO3 membranes exhibit optical properties comparable to those of bulk single crystals. We extend this approach to the metallic ferromagnet La0.7Sr0.3MnO3, obtaining crack-free membranes on Si that preserve ferromagnetism and metallicity.

items.title: The 1d Stochastic Dirac Operator
items.summary: We introduce a random Dirac operator on $L^2(\mathbb{R},\mathbb{R}^2)$ that we call $1d$ Stochastic Dirac Operator and which is indexed by two parameters $κ_0,κ$. In two companion articles, we show that this operator arises generically as the small disorder limit of one-dimensional random Schrödinger operators, thus revealing a universal behavior. In the present paper, we provide a detailed construction of this singular operator, and investigate its spectral properties. In particular, we show that its spectrum is either absolutely continuous when $κ= 0$, or pure point when $κ>0$. In the latter case, we show that the shape of the eigenfunctions is given by the exponential of a two sided Brownian motion with drift, in connection with a result of Rifkind and Virág. Finally, we establish a delicate convergence result of the sequence of eigenvalues / eigenfunctions from the finite-volume operator to the infinite-volume one.

items.title: Single-Crystal Growth, Structure, and Physical Properties of Yb2MoO6
items.summary: Rare-earth molybdates are functional oxides of considerable interest because their structural and chemical flexibility enables diverse magnetic, electronic, and optical behavior. Here, millimeter-sized single crystals of $Yb_2MoO_6$ are synthesized, their crystal structure determined and physical properties investigated. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction confirms the formation of $Yb_2MoO_6$ and yielded lattice parameters of $a = 16.228(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, $b = 10.901(3)$ $\mathring{A}$, and $c = 5.286(2)$ $\mathring{A}$, in good agreement with previously reported neutron powder diffraction data. Scanning electron microscopy and energy-dispersive spectroscopy show a Yb:Mo ratio close to the expected 2:1 stoichiometry. Optical measurements based on diffuse-reflectance spectra and Tauc analysis yield an estimated optical gap of $\sim 3.28$ eV under the direct-allowed transition assumption. Magnetic susceptibility measurements reveal Curie-Weiss-like paramagnetic behavior, with an effective magnetic moment of $μ_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 4.2μ_B$ per Yb and an apparent Weiss temperature of $θ\approx -65.7$ K, consistent with possible antiferromagnetic interactions or correlations, with no clear magnetic-ordering transition observed down to 10 K. These results establish the growth of $Yb_2MoO_6$ single crystals and provide initial insight into their structural, optical, and magnetic properties.

items.title: Non-Abelian quantum Hall states at strong Landau level mixing: finding anyons with first-principles AI
items.summary: Non-Abelian anyons, strange particles forming the basis of fault-tolerant topological quantum computing, are predicted to emerge in fractional quantum Hall states at even-denominator filling factors. Identifying which topological order is realized has proven to be a challenging problem that requires an accurate, non-perturbative treatment of realistic Landau level mixing, which has so far been missing from theoretical studies. Here we present the first complete solution of non-Abelian quantum Hall problem that includes all electrons and all Landau levels, for spin-polarized electrons at filling factor $ν= 3/2$. We develop a momentum-resolved neural-network variational wave function, optimized solely on the microscopic Hamiltonian, which gives direct access to the topologically degenerate ground states. Without any physics input about the expected outcome, it discovers a degenerate ground-state manifold whose entanglement reveals anyons with quantum dimension $\sqrt{2}$, the hallmark of Ising-type non-Abelian order. By directly computing the overlap with trial wave functions, we further show that Landau level mixing favors the anti-Pfaffian over other candidate states. Our results demonstrate the power of neural-network wave functions in finding and characterizing non-Abelian anyons from first principles, in regimes of strong Landau level mixing, relevant to many recent experiments.

items.title: A Symmetry-Stratified Framework for Phase Transitions: Thermodynamic States, Critical Dynamics, and Spectral Mechanical Signatures
items.summary: Structural symmetry, thermodynamic phase stability, and elastic-wave response provide related but distinct descriptions of a transforming solid. We formulate a symmetry-stratified framework that connects these descriptions through a finite-dimensional internal state and a parent-invariant free energy. Stabilizers classify structural states, whereas free-energy comparisons and stability conditions determine equilibrium branches and dissipative evolution. Equivariance ensures that the frozen elastic tangent inherits the structural stabilizer. Equality requires additional identifiability conditions. Little-group representations and degenerate perturbation theory then determine whether an acoustic doublet splits and the first nonzero splitting order $p$. On a selected continuous branch with order-parameter exponent $β$, a regular, observable acoustic gap scales as $|t|^{pβ}$, provided critical self-energies and structural relaxation do not dominate the measurement. Explicit tensorial and cubic-to-tetragonal realizations yield linear and quadratic splitting channels, together with directionally protected degeneracies. Separate numerical benchmarks examine free-energy reconstruction, coexistence, elastic compatibility, finite-temperature spectra, and controlled critical readouts. Reanalysis of NiTi measurements illustrates effective elastic degeneracy, thermal-history dependence, and the predictive value of independently measured phase fractions. Most importantly, the framework identifies the constitutive and measurement assumptions required to infer structural changes from mechanical spectra.

items.title: A Resolution to the Marcus-Rehm-Weller Paradox in Electron Transfer
items.summary: Marcus theory famously predicts that electron-transfer rates decrease once the thermodynamic driving force exceeds the reorganization energy. Yet many systems instead exhibit Rehm-Weller kinetics, characterized by rate saturation rather than decrease. Here we show that these apparently contradictory phenomenologies can emerge as opposite physical limits of the same two-state harmonic Hamiltonian. In the normal region, the model recovers both Marcus and Rehm-Weller behavior. In the inverted region, however, it predicts Marcus's decreasing rate in the nonadiabatic limit but Rehm-Weller saturation in the adiabatic limit. Using physically plausible reorganization energies and electronic coupling values, we show that Rehm-Weller's data can be quantitatively reproduced within a microscopic quantum model. Finally, we note that the model predicts three regions of adiabatic electron transfer: (1) a normal region with kinetics governed by an effective reorganization energy, (2) a finite region of barrierless transfer, and (3) a region in which the correspondence between diabatic and adiabatic states is reversed, suppressing the Marcus rate.

items.title: Tunable source of entangled microwaves by nonlinear scattering of magnons
items.summary: We propose a route to prepare entangled states of microwaves propagating in spatially separated transmission lines using the intrinsic nonlinear dynamics of ferromagnetic spin waves (magnons). We first show that a driven magnon mode can produce entangled magnon pairs at low temperatures by spontaneous parametric down-conversion enabled by three-magnon processes. The anisotropic magnon properties in thin films result in strict phase-matching conditions which allow only a well-defined pair of magnon modes to be amplified. This mode selectivity allows to out-couple each amplified mode to an independent microwave transmission line, producing non-degenerate propagating microwave entanglement with current experimental parameters. In addition, we prove that the frequency difference between the two entangled microwaves can be dynamically tuned across a few-GHz range by changing the orientation of a bias magnetic field. Our figures of merit - .g., the amount of microwave entanglement - can be largely improved by optimizing material and geometry. Our work establishes that quantum states of propagating magnons can be created by their nonlinear dynamics alone, and opens a pathway toward integrating magnons in hybrid quantum platforms.

items.title: Symmetries, correlation functions, and entanglement of general quantum Motzkin spin-chains
items.summary: Motzkin spin-chains, which include `colorless' (integer spin $s=1$) and `colorful' ($s \geq 2$) variants, are one-dimensional (1D) local integer spin models notable for their lack of a conformal field theory (CFT) description of their low-energy physics, despite being gapless. The colorful variants are particularly unusual, as they exhibit power-law violation of the area-law of entanglement entropy (as $\sqrt{n}$ in system size $n$), rather than a logarithmic violation as seen in a CFT. In this work, we analytically discover several unique properties of these models, potentially suggesting a new universality class for their low-energy physics. We identify a complex structure of symmetries and unexpected scaling behavior in spin-spin correlations, which deviate from known 1D universality classes. Specifically, the $s=1$ chain exhibits $U(1)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking and ferromagnetic order. Meanwhile, the $s \geq 2$ chains do not appear to spontaneously break any symmetries, but display quasi-long-range algebraic order with power-law decaying correlations, inconsistent with standard Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) critical exponents. We also derive asymptotic scaling expressions, with explicit additive constants, for entanglement measures in both colorless and colorful chains, generalizing previous results of Movassagh [J. Math Phys. (2017)], while providing benchmarks for potential quantum simulation experiments. The $\sqrt{n}$ entanglement scaling implies that any matrix-product-state description of these ground states requires bond dimension $e^{Ω(\sqrt{n})}$; this superpolynomial cost of the standard 1D tensor-network toolkit, along with the analytical tractability of their ground state properties, positions Motzkin spin chains as intriguing testbeds for quantum simulation of many-body physics.

items.title: Foresight-dependent entropy production in stochastic two-agent dynamics
items.summary: Nonreciprocal interactions can break detailed balance by sustaining stationary probability currents. We ask whether such currents can also emerge when agents' immediate coordination preferences are reciprocal but their adjustment rules result from forward-looking optimization. We study a minimal stochastic linear--quadratic game in which two agents control noisy scalar states and minimize individual discounted costs in a full-information feedback Nash equilibrium. The optimized controls yield an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process whose stationary current, entropy production, and inter-agent information flow follow exactly from the Nash feedback. For reciprocal coordination with unequal self-anchoring, the drift asymmetry first appears at order $τ^5$, where $τ$ is the planning timescale, and the normalized entropy production scales as $τ^8$. We trace this delay to one mechanism: the asymmetry is set by the mismatch between the agents' value-function curvatures along the coordinate each does not control. At leading order this equals the mismatch of the corresponding cost curvatures, which instantaneous incentives cannot see and which the coordination cost fixes to zero; unequal persistence of the partners' fluctuations generates a value-function mismatch at order $τ^3$, postponing the asymmetry to fifth order, while a direct stake in the partner's state restores a cubic law. The normalized information flow, of order $τ^4$, identifies the weakly anchored agent as the one that tracks its partner. For conformist--contrarian coupling, normalized entropy production starts from a nonzero limit and initially decreases as $τ^2$; for equal anchoring, we prove that its long-foresight limit lies below the short-foresight value and that the stationary mutual-information flow vanishes. Numerical solutions of the full Nash equations confirm these laws.

items.title: Assessing the Transferability of General-Purpose MachineLearning Interatomic Potentials for Heterogeneous Catalysis with HetCat26
items.summary: Foundation machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) promise near-density functional theory (DFT) accuracy across broad areas of chemistry and materials science. However, their performance in describing systems and processes relevant to heterogeneous catalysis remains underexplored. Here, we introduce HetCat26, a collection of benchmark tests designed to assess pre-trained MLIPs across key aspects of catalytic modeling, including surface energetics, metal-metal oxide interactions, adsorption, and catalytic reaction networks. Evaluating eighteen foundation models, we find that performance on existing general materials benchmarks is only weakly predictive of performance on HetCat26; transferability to heterogeneous catalysis cannot be inferred from these general benchmarks. Across the benchmark tests, current models describe surface energetics and, perhaps surprisingly, reaction barriers well, whereas larger errors are observed for adsorption, and DFT site preferences are often not reproduced. Three models, eSEN-30M-OAM, SevenNet-Omni-i12 and MACE-MH-1-OMAT, nevertheless achieve high accuracy across the properties evaluated. Beyond model benchmarking, HetCat26 highlights the importance of training data consistency: PBE and PBE+U calculations should not be mixed within a training set. Overall, we identify challenges limiting the transferability of current foundation MLIPs to heterogeneous catalysis and, more broadly, to chemical reactions at interfaces, providing guidance for the development of the next generation of foundation models.

items.title: Euler Topological Metals in 1D
items.summary: We give a rigorous one-dimensional formulation of Kane's transport proposal for probing the Euler characteristic of a Fermi sea. For a clean, translation-invariant continuum Hamiltonian with real-analytic dispersion, a Fermi sea confined to a finite momentum range, and nonzero Fermi velocity at every Fermi point, we analyze a particular regularized transport response (obtained by tracing over the Fermi sea) and prove that its large-time limit equals the Euler characteristic. We derive an explicit finite-time formula, show that quantization requires the large-time limit, and obtain a convergence rate under additional nonstationarity assumptions. We also prove the lattice analog, where the commutator of the spatial switch with its time evolution is trace-class and a completely filled band contributes zero. Finite-volume calculations illustrate the prescribed order of the thermodynamic and large-time limits.

items.title: The phase diagram of fluid hydrogen near melting from machine-learned interatomic potentials trained on quantum Monte Carlo
items.summary: Dissociation of molecular hydrogen increasing temperature or pressure may either occur gradually or abruptly, via a phase transition. Despite considerable experimental and theoretical efforts, the phase diagram of dense hydrogen at temperatures above solid melting is not precisely known. Here, we perform classical and quantum Path Integral molecular dynamics simulations of dense hydrogen using two machine-learned interatomic potentials both trained on quantum Monte Carlo energies and forces. The resulting phase diagram is constructed using state-of-the-art techniques. Both models show a first-order phase transition from the molecular to the atomic liquid terminating in critical points whose locations were determined using finite-size scaling techniques. Triple points, located at the highest temperature of the melting curve, are found at the intersection of the liquid-liquid lines with the melting curve and should lead to clear signatures in ramp compression experiments.

items.title: Geometric control of diffusive relaxation: spectral design, transport bounds and transverse mode isolation
items.summary: Geometric confinement changes both thermal relaxation and heat throughput, but these effects need not be governed by the same conduction path. We establish a distinction between serial and parallel geometries for passive, homogeneous Fourier conductors at fixed material properties, volume and length. For a reduced variable-area conductor, two logarithmic shape harmonics independently tune two selected Bloch-rate pairs, and exact local transport level sets permit spectral redistribution at fixed effective diffusivity. A nonperturbative weighted Poincaré bound, however, requires the effective axial diffusivity to vanish if the first positive insulated rate tends to zero at fixed length. This obstruction is avoided by continuous parallel paths with weak transverse exchange. Capacity-weighted networks identify the exchange mechanism, and a three-dimensional product domain provides an exact bulk realization. Its axial conductance remains $κV/L^2$, while exactly one positive insulated rate vanishes and the next approaches a positive limit set by axial, chamber and neck diffusion. The slow rate is asymptotically the transverse neck conductance times the sum of inverse chamber capacities. Spectral projection estimates translate this separation into a preparation- and readout-dependent observation window. The result is metastable retention of a temperature contrast under insulated conditions, not a second equilibrium state. It identifies when geometrical control of internal equilibration can be separated from macroscopic heat transport.

items.title: Projected evolution of quantum gates for circuit simulation with matrix product states
items.summary: Tensor networks and specifically matrix product states (MPS) enable feasible classical quantum circuit simulation when entanglement remains compressible, but for this, gate updates must balance accuracy, representation size, and runtime. Conventional methods incorporate a complete gate into the MPS before compressing enlarged bonds. Here, we instead use lessons from the time-dependent variational principle (TDVP) to analyze the projected action of each gate on the MPS by reducing it to a continuous generator path. We establish the spatial and state-space structure of this projected evolution and show that both the fixed-rank and two-site actions are confined to a contiguous window spanned by the gate while retaining boundary information from the surrounding MPS. Within this window characterization, we delineate when the instantaneous two-site action is exact and when variational directions can block it completely. Using standard nearest-point-projection geometry, we also show that fixed-rank TDVP and the local nearest fixed-rank projection of the exact gate endpoint agree to first order. We implement the gate-window restriction with rank-adaptive two-site TDVP and test both the projected update and a hybrid method that reserves it for long-range gates. Across the circuit benchmarks, these implementations incur runtime overhead and show no consistent accuracy--cost advantage over the tested baseline methods. The resulting framework provides a gate-specific structural analysis and a tested implementation together with explicit limits on its practical performance.

items.title: Emergence and Detection of Surface altermagnetism in KV$_2$Se$_2$O
items.summary: We demonstrate the recent concept of emergent surface altermagnetism through its unique signatures in KV$_2$Se$_2$O. We show that for bulk antiferromagnetically ordered KV$_2$Se$_2$O, the (001) surface exhibits $d$-wave altermagnetism. Our results fully explain the recent seemingly contradicgting experimental evidence, independently showing both an antiferromagnetically ordered bulk from neutron diffraction, and $d$-wave spin splitting from photoemission spectroscopy. To fully verify this conecept, we predict, as a key experimental signature, a large nonlinear Edelstein response, which is localized at the surface, and follows the $d$-wave altermagnetic symmetry. These results are not only relevant for the metallic and room-temperature magnet KV$_2$Se$_2$O, but also for several other Lieb lattice systems. Our work expands the pool of techniques that can be used to detect altermagnetism emerging at the surfaces of antiferromagnets.

items.title: \textsc{Max-Cut} on Token Graphs
items.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, is the graph, $F_k(G)$, whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of vertices of $G$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. The phase-reconstruction problem for Heisenberg antiferromagnets in physics can be rephrased as a Max-Cut problem on token graphs. Motivated by this, we study the Max-Cut problem on token graphs, mainly when all edges are assigned the same weight. Our main focus is to bound $m(F_k(G))$ in terms of $m(G)$. We prove that $m(F_k(G))\geq\binom{n-2}{k-1}m(G)$, and that this bound is tight up to a multiplicative factor of $1+O(k/n)$; in the case when $k=c \cdot n$ for some constant $0 < c < 1$, we provide an example where this bound is off by a multiplicative constant factor. We also show bounds for $m(F_k(G))$ for various classes of graphs $G$. Finally, we consider the algorithmic complexity of finding $m(F_k(G))$, showing it to be NP-complete for a constant $k$, and giving evidence that, when the weights take finitely many values, it is not NP-hard for $k\geq n^δ$ for any constant $δ>0$.

items.title: Machine Learning-Driven High-Throughput Screening of Equimolar and Non-Equimolar High-Entropy Carbides
items.summary: Search for optimal compositions among high-entropy ceramics are challenging due to large composition space, which are unable to test either experimentally or by \textit{ab initio} calculations. Here we present a high-throughput screening for equimolar and non-equimolar high-entropy carbides (HEC) among group IVB and VB transition metals (Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta). Large Atomistic Model MACE, and deep learning based interatomic potential DeePMD trained on \textit{ab initio}-based dataset of structures are used to effectively screen over the thousands of potential non-equimolar compositions among high-entropy carbides of Ti, Zr, Hf, V, Nb and Ta transition metals. A set of both equimolar and non-equimolar HECs are predicted to be stable in order to further synthesize those compositions based on the predictions.

items.title: Learning Integer Winding Evolution Times in Quantum Phase Estimation
items.summary: Learning a Hamiltonian evolution time in Quantum Phase Estimation that produces phase distributions with low Shannon entropy circumvents the fundamental limit of digitization error of phase, independent of the number of phase qubits of accuracy. By introducing an optimization loop to minimize the Shannon entropy of measured eigenvalues produced by a QPE quantum circuit, minimum eigenvalue computation accuracy is greatly improved, which we show numerically on quantum magnet models. This technique works because standard QPE has a natural correspondence between entropy of the phase distribution and the analog accuracy of the minimum eigenvalue phase. This introduces for the first time a type of parameter learning to QPE, which makes near term practicality of QPE for fundamental sciences more feasible by using shorter depth QPE circuits.

items.title: A plane-wave auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo study of silicon point defects
items.summary: Accurately predicting the energetics of point defects remains a formidable challenge in computational materials science. For the tetrahedral silicon self-interstitial, for example, previous periodic coupled-cluster [CCSD(T)] and diffusion Monte Carlo (DMC) calculations disagree by about 1.2 eV. Here, we present formation energies of silicon self-interstitials and vacancies using auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (AFQMC) in a plane-wave basis formulated within the projector-augmented wave framework, and compare them with the random-phase approximation (RPA) and CCSD(T). Using 16- and 64-atom cells, we demonstrate that an RPA-based correction effectively removes the two-body finite-size errors that remain after twist averaging in AFQMC for bulk silicon and for the dumbbell and hexagonal self-interstitials. With this correction, we obtain formation energies of 4.4 eV and 4.6 eV for these two self-interstitials in 16-atom cells, in good agreement with DMC and transcorrelated coupled-cluster results. For the tetrahedral interstitial and the Jahn--Teller-distorted vacancy, 16-atom cells are too small to obtain realistic formation energies; in 64-atom cells, we obtain 5.7 eV and 5.2 eV, respectively. With identical setups in 16-atom cells, CCSD(T) yields systematically lower formation energies than AFQMC, with the largest difference, 250 meV, for the tetrahedral interstitial. Our results indicate that the earlier overestimation of CCSD(T) for the tetrahedral interstitial stems from the finite-size treatment in the coupled-cluster workflow rather than from multi-configurational character of the defect.

items.title: Optimal parameterization of nonequilibrium generalized master equations from discrete-time experimental data
items.summary: Kinetic analyses of experiments often require coarse-grained descriptions, but complex systems rarely conform to the widely used modeling assumptions of Markovianity and thermodynamic equilibrium. Memory is indeed a general and often inevitable consequence of coarse-graining. Markov state models (MSMs) are a popular choice of coarse-grained description, but require microstate assignments---which are rarely experimentally tunable---to macrostates that minimize memory. Generalized master equations (GMEs) circumvent this limitation of MSMs by explicitly capturing memory. However, GMEs are difficult to parameterize and usually formally approximate in the experimentally relevant discrete-time setting. Here we introduce a maximum-likelihood-based procedure to parameterize formally exact, physically feasible, discrete-time generalized master equations from experiments and simulations in and out of equilibrium. By adapting algorithms typically used in optimal transport, we construct physical-constraint-satisfying conditional-maximum-likelihood estimators of both exact Nakajima-Zwanzig memory kernels and time-convolutionless GME propagators in discrete time. Applying these estimators to three examples---experimental recordings of Förster resonance energy transfer in an ion channel, experimental nanoparticle tracking of a processive molecular motor, and simulated folding of a benchmark protein domain---we recover kinetic parameters including relaxation rates, irreversibilities, dwell times, and first-passage times. These results establish discrete-time GMEs as a physically and statistically principled alternative to MSMs for kinetic analyses of experimental and simulated biomolecular systems.

items.title: Where electrons conduct and where to change it: gauge-invariant sensitivities and the networks of sensitive bonds
items.summary: Where is the electrical current carried in a disordered solid, and where would a local change alter it? The two questions differ. We answer the second exactly: the derivative of the Kubo-Greenwood conductivity with respect to the Hamiltonian is gauge invariant and gives the response to any local change. The construction applies to any Hamiltonian. We try it on amorphous silicon, with tight-binding cells of up to 10000 atoms and density-functional cells of up to 512 atoms, and compare it with three ways of allocating the conductivity: the space-projected conductivity (SPC), KuboMap, and the local density of states (LDOS). KuboMap follows the LDOS closely (median Spearman correlation 0.97). The sensitivity does not. It ranks the response to an on-site shift accurately and the response to removing an atom poorly, and it transfers between Hamiltonians less well than the other maps. The most sensitive bonds form connected clusters. In three large networks they are tree-like filaments of 24 to 38 atoms in the valence tail and looped networks deeper in the gap; the excess over an LDOS-weighted random selection reaches 48 standard deviations and appears only when the broadening spans about five level spacings. The filament overlaps the tail eigenstate with the most weight on it, and one of the leading conduction channels, far more than a random cluster does, but no single state or channel explains it. The networks are largely lost in thermal snapshots at 300 K. Where the conductivity is carried and where it responds are different problems: local transport maps are useful for the first and limited for the second.

items.title: Mixtures of a fluid with competing interactions and a simple solvent near a hard wall
items.summary: We study a binary mixture of soft particles near a planar surface. The main component interacts through a competing short-range attraction and long-range repulsion (SALR) potential, modelled by a sum of three Yukawa terms, while the solvent and the cross interactions are described by two Yukawa terms. Using a field-theoretical mean-field approach we derive the coupled equations for the density profiles of both species, formulate the contact theorem for the two-component system, and obtain closed-form profiles in the mesoscopically homogeneous region by linearizing the theory and solving the associated eigenvalue problem. Their amplitudes are fixed by exact boundary conditions following from the continuity of the Yukawa potentials at the wall, which supply as many relations as there are unknowns. Although these conditions are implicit in the derivation of the contact theorem, they have not previously been used to fix the amplitudes of the linearized profiles, and they bring those profiles into quantitative agreement with the nonlinear solution. The equations are solved numerically for a fluid confined by hard walls. The theory predicts mixing of the two species far from the surface at high temperatures, and their microphase separation into alternating layers upon cooling or upon increasing the density. The mean-field profiles agree well with molecular dynamics data once the mean-field overestimate of the onset temperature of microsegregation is taken into account, and the analytical ones reproduce them closely except in the immediate vicinity of the wall.

items.title: Chiral Phonons Protected by Symmetry in a Strongly Anharmonic Helical Material
items.summary: How chiral phonons survive anharmonic phonon-phonon interactions, which underpin lattice dynamics at finite temperature, remains poorly understood. Using an ab initio many-body approach, we study crystalline tellurium (Te), a strongly anharmonic helical crystal. We show that rotational symmetries in Te impose pseudoangular momentum selection rules on phonon-phonon interactions, restricting mode mixing and scattering at rotationally invariant symmetry points in the Brillouin zone. These symmetries protect the circular polarization of vibrational modes at finite temperature but not their lifetimes such that the dynamic chirality of handed vibrational modes persists to 600 K, even as lifetimes drop sharply. We find that the temperature-dependence of angular momentum generated by a thermal gradient is governed by lifetimes rather than chirality, decreasing by two orders of magnitude between 10 and 600 K.

items.title: Impact of Surface Preparation on the Propulsion of Catalytic Janus Colloids and Implications for Reproducibility
items.summary: Platinum-coated polystyrene (PS) Janus particles (JPs) propelled by the catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) are a widely used model system for active matter, yet reported speeds for similar particles and fuel concentrations differ by more than an order of magnitude. Broad adoption of these materials requires increasing consistency in the preparation and achieving improved repeatability in their behavior. Herein, we focused on two routine, but rarely reported, preparation steps that we found to alter the particle speed. First, we found that pre-exposing the platinum cap to H2O2 before cell assembly increased the mean speed by a factor of 2.4. The size of this effect depended on batch history, where an aged batch responded strongly, while a freshly prepared batch sped up by only 16%. Second, we found that plasma cleaning of the glass substrate decreased the speed 2.7 times. In a 120 $μ$m cell the suppression was the same at both walls even when only one wall was treated. The suppression grew with the treated glass area per unit fluid volume, which pointed to species released into the bulk solution rather than to a change at the wall. Plasma-cleaned glass released more ions into water than untreated glass, and XPS detected an ionic metal fluoride on the plasma-cleaned surface. A model in which the released ions lower the speed through the solution conductivity reproduced the measured speeds in all four cell geometries. Of the 17 published studies compared here, pre-activation is reported in only four studies and substrate cleaning in only six studies. We propose a minimum reporting standard for the preparation and associated speed measurements of catalytic Janus particles.

items.title: Certified Discovery of Quantum Phase Diagrams
items.summary: Can a machine provably discover new quantum phases of matter? We show that the answer is yes under physically motivated assumptions. For any smooth family of geometrically local Hamiltonians, we construct an efficient quantum algorithm that outputs the phase diagram to prescribed accuracy and provides a verifiable certificate for every transition it reports. The algorithm takes as input only a classical description of the family together with unverified preparations of reference ground states; no order parameter, symmetry-breaking pattern, or training data are supplied. It succeeds provided that at least one preparation is correct in each gapped region of parameter space. The algorithm explores parameter space by quasi-adiabatically or adiabatically transporting each reference state, detecting the approach of a phase boundary by tapping the transported state with a frequency-filtered local probe: excitations created by the probe witness the closing of the energy gap. We prove that the gap closing for continuous phase transitions can always be detected using the frequency-filtered gradient of the Hamiltonian. The gap-detecting measurement is gentle, so when the ground state is unique a single reusable copy of each reference ground state supports the full exploration (for degenerate ground states, polynomially many copies suffice). The quantum algorithm runs in polynomial time at inverse-polynomial gap resolution. We also give a classical algorithm that runs in quasipolynomial time at constant gap resolution. Numerical experiments demonstrate how our algorithm accurately determines the phase structure of several model quantum systems.

items.title: $C_T$ and $C_J$ of general scalar--fermion conformal field theories in $d=4-ε$
items.summary: We compute $C_T$ and $C_J$, the coefficients of the stress-tensor and conserved-current two-point functions, to order $ε^3$ at any fixed point of the general renormalizable theory of scalars and fermions in $d=4-ε$. We give explicit results for the chiral Ising, XY and Heisenberg models and for fixed points with emergent supersymmetry in $d=3$. In theories without a four-dimensional counterpart, fermion loops with an odd number of Yukawa vertices contribute at order $ε^3$ through traces whose continuation away from $d=3$ is ambiguous; we fix it with $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetry, by computing the two-point functions of the supercurrent and of the fermionic partner of a flavor current to four loops. In $d=3$, Padé approximants closely reproduce the exact $C_T$ of the $\mathcal N=2$ super-Ising model. We estimate the universal conductivity at the charge-density-wave, Kekulé and Néel transitions of graphene to be $σ/σ_{\rm free}\approx0.91$, $0.79$--$0.83$ and $0.64$--$0.74$, and show that the exact conductivity at the supersymmetric transition on the surface of a topological insulator is $σ/σ_{\rm free}=\frac{9}{10}\,C_T/C_{T,\rm free}\approx0.654$, $10\%$ below the value previously reported.

items.title: Quantum many-body scars and zero modes in the spin-1 Kitaev chain
items.summary: We study the spin-1 Kitaev chain and, by analyzing its Hilbert-space connectivity in the Cartesian basis, show that it hosts an exponentially large number of exact zero-energy modes protected by chiral symmetry. For even-length periodic chains, their count is lower-bounded by the Jacobsthal number $(2^{L+1}+1)/3$, where $L$ is the chain length. We then construct an exponentially large number ($2^{L/2}$) of zero modes with an analytic expression that have a maximally mixed density matrix for a contiguous bipartition using the operator-state mapping. We further identify an embedded tight-binding structure governing defect dynamics that supports PXP-like quantum many-body scars (QMBS) in multiple sectors previously not reported. The associated forward-scattering approximation (FSA) Hamiltonian takes a universal form across the scarred sectors studied. A simple physical picture of defects propagating between walls provides an intuitive description of these dynamics and a structural guide to identifying sectors with fidelity revivals, while its limitations point to additional scarring mechanisms.

items.title: Topological (in)equivalence encoded in zeros of wavefunction overlaps
items.summary: Topological equivalence between two gapped band structures is determined by whether their occupied states can be continuously deformed into one another without closing the energy gap or breaking the protecting symmetries. We show that this relative topology can be read directly from the overlap matrix between the two occupied subspaces, in a way that treats Chern and $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariants within a single framework. The determinant of the overlap matrix defines a global section of a line bundle over the Brillouin zone, which vanishes at the momenta where the map between the subspaces fails to be invertible. A singular connection, whose curvature is concentrated at these zeros, assigns each zero an integer charge given by its phase winding. In two-dimensional class A, the total charge equals the difference between the Chern numbers of the two systems. In class AII, time reversal pairs zeros of opposite charge, and the relative $\mathbb{Z}_2$ invariant is the parity of the total charge in half the Brillouin zone; the Kane-Mele Pfaffian is recovered as a special case. The zeros coincide with the gap closings of an interpolation between the two systems, and crystalline symmetries constrain their positions and charges. We illustrate the construction in the Haldane, Kane-Mele, and Qi-Wu-Zhang models, including cases where rotation symmetry alone enforces the zeros.

items.title: Anyon Coherent States in Fractional Chern Insulators
items.summary: In fractional quantum Hall (FQH) systems, coherent anyonic excitations are the natural entities for describing anyon dynamics, their interactions, and braiding, yet no general expression for their wavefunctions is known beyond Laughlin's quasiholes. We introduce a systematic, operator-based construction of maximally-localized wavefunctions of anyons of either charge in FQH states and fractional Chern insulators, including those in non-ideal, non-vortexable bands. We find that these wavefunctions describe coherent quasiparticles: zero modes of local annihilation operators that saturate projected-density uncertainty bounds. These coherent states owe their existence to a nontrivial topology of the anyon band, with the winding of their Bloch coefficients encoding an anyon band's Chern number. As such, their guiding centers exist anywhere within the lattice, and their mutual overlaps decay as Gaussians determined by the effective magnetic length of the anyon band.

items.title: Passive memories beyond the Ising model: from SFQ to GKP
items.summary: Self-correcting quantum memories are spin Hamiltonians that aim to generalize the classical memory of the magnetic hard disk (i.e. ferromagnetic Ising model) to protect against both bit flips and phase flips. Beyond the magnetic hard disk, there are other passive classical memories that are used in modern computers, notably: the flash memory in laptops (which traps charge on a conducting island), and the flux storage loop in single-flux quantum (SFQ) logic (which traps flux in a superconducting loop). In this paper we review how storage and writing work in these two classical memories, drawing analogies to the charge qubit and the flux qubit. Protection in these systems derives not from scaling a lattice to the thermodynamic limit, but from a large, tunable energy barrier that separates codewords during memory, yet can be suppressed during a write. Towards protecting a qubit: We introduce a 2D ``floating XY model'' that combines the exponential (phase-flip) protection of the floating charge island with the polynomial (bit-flip) protection of the ferromagnetic XY model. We also study a self-dual superconducting circuit that hosts GKP codewords as symmetry-broken ground states of a $\mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2 $-symmetric circuit, and discuss its protection and limitations.

items.title: Chern Numbers from Symmetry-Enforced Zeros and Dispersion Shifts
items.summary: Wave-function zeros and their local vorticities provide a complementary characterization of Chern topology to more commonly used Berry-curvature formulations. Using wave-function overlaps between a Chern band and freely chosen reference states, we show that crystalline symmetry can enforce their zeros and fix their vorticities modulo the rotation order from the angular momenta of the band and reference state. We further show that weak local perturbations produce band-dispersion shifts proportional to the absolute square of the overlap, allowing its zeros and local structure to be read off directly from the dispersion. Combined with crystalline symmetry, this can identify Chern topology without measuring wave-function phases. Our construction applies to multicomponent and multiband wave functions and allows reference states whose momentum-space representation may vanish at some momenta. This permits compact localized states to be used directly as reference states and makes use of their known real- and momentum-space properties in flat-band systems. The dispersion shift near an overlap zero further provides a lower bound on the quantum metric at the zero.

items.title: The Clifford Hierarchy from Clifford Stabilizers in 2D
items.summary: The Bravyi-König theorem limits the constant-depth logical gates of 2D topological Pauli stabilizer codes to be in the Clifford group. Known qubit codes with Clifford stabilizers exceed it by only one level of the Clifford hierarchy, and this was conjectured to hold generally. We show that this bound can be completely bypassed, and that topological codes with Clifford stabilizers in 2D can realize transversal logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy. We present two explicit constructions of codes based on copies of the quantum doubles of $D_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_2$, with $k$ logical qubits and a logical $C^{k-1}Z$ gate, which is at level $k$ of the Clifford hierarchy. The physical circuits realizing the gates consist only of physical $Z$ or $CZ$ gates. The main new ingredient comes from the logical encoding, which depends crucially on non-Abelian group multiplication.

items.title: First order vortex-unbinding transition in 2D topological superconductors
items.summary: We study the fate of the Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT) transition in a two-dimensional topological superconductor whose vortex cores each host an isolated Majorana zero mode, energetically well separated from the bulk gap and other bound states of the vortex. When the Majorana localization length $ξ_F$ exceeds the vortex core size $ξ$, nearby vortices acquire an additional short-range attractive channel from Majorana hybridization, modifying the vortex-antivortex interaction at short distances and generating a metastable minimum in the two-vortex free energy above the nominal $T_{BKT}$. We construct an effective field theory for the resulting dilute vortex gas, coupling the ordinary BKT phase field to an additional field encoding the Majorana-mediated interaction, and show, using renormalization-group and instanton methods, that this hybridization can drive the transition first order, with the metastable phase decaying at an exponentially small rate. We propose an array of Josephson-coupled $p+ip$ superconducting islands as a microscopic platform realizing the required hierarchy of scales. Finally, we discuss experimental signatures of this first-order transition, in particular a hysteresis loop whose width is set by the coexistence window.

items.title: Umklapp-enhanced high-$T_c$ topological superconductivity mediated by magnons in $p$-wave magnets
items.summary: We show that magnon exchange can induce nodal topological superconductivity in a microscopic model of a $p$-wave magnet. Solving the weak-coupling multiband gap equation for itinerant electrons exchange-coupled to localized spins, we find a nodal $p$-wave gap and a critical temperature that rises sharply as the Fermi surface approaches the magnetic Brillouin-zone boundary. In this regime, small-reduced-momentum magnons can scatter electrons between Fermi-surface segments on opposite sides of the zone. These Umklapp processes enhance pairing because the contributions from different sites in the magnetic unit cell cancel less in their electron-magnon vertices than in those for ordinary scattering at comparable reduced momenta. Momentum-resolved winding numbers predict zero-energy Majorana flat bands at symmetry-preserving edges where the bulk nodes project to distinct momenta.

items.title: Exact Parent Hamiltonians for Partially Magnetized Chiral Spin Liquids
items.summary: Chiral spin liquids (CSLs) are paradigmatic fractionalized phases, yet simple exact parent Hamiltonians for them remain scarce. In this work, we construct exact spin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs realizing various bosonic topological orders. Our construction relies on an exact Hubbard-type parent Hamiltonian for bosonic lattice fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, valid at arbitrary repulsive interaction strengths. Taking the on-site repulsion to infinity and applying local boson-spin mappings yields exact parent Hamiltonians for the CSLs. Our two-spin construction generalizes the Kalmeyer-Laughlin spin Hamiltonian to a broader class of bosonic FQH model states, including Abelian states and non-Abelian parton states. We derive controlled microscopic realizations of these two-spin Hamiltonians via second-order superexchange in generalized spinful Hofstadter-Hubbard models with tailored hoppings and interactions. With more general local constraints and interactions, boson-spin mappings yield exact higher-spin and multispin parent Hamiltonians for partially magnetized CSLs.

items.title: Low-energy states of a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chain connected perpendicularly to a metallic lead
items.summary: Recently, Su-Schrieffer-Heeger chains (SSHCs) coupled to metallic leads have attracted attention. In particular Martínez {\it et al.} [Phys. Rev. Res. {\bf 8}, 043118 (2026)] studied a topological SSHC connected at one of its ends perpendicularly to a metallic lead modeled by a tight-binding chain. Here, we extend their results by incorporating the finite-size splitting of the end modes of the isolated SSHC, which are determined analytically with high accuracy. We also derive simple analytical expressions, valid in the low-energy regime, for the zero-temperature conductance through the lead and the relevant spectral densities. We find that, when the chemical potential coincides with that of the half-filled SSHC, the conductance reaches its maximum value, equal to that of the lead in the absence of the SSHC. By contrast, the conductance vanishes when the chemical potential is shifted by an amount equal to half the end-mode splitting.

items.title: Exact Fractional Chern Insulators from Hubbard Interactions
items.summary: Laughlin's wavefunction and its parent interaction, Haldane's pseudopotential, underpin our analytic understanding of fractional quantum Hall effect. They are an exact pair in the sense that the wavefunction is the unique, zero-energy ground state of its frustration-free parent Hamiltonian. In this work, we propose exact pairs of many-body wavefunctions for fractional Chern insulators in tight binding models with onsite Hubbard interactions as their parents. The key to our construction is introduction of a Landau-dual Chern band, a multi-orbital Chern band obtained from directly sampling the spin-$s$ Dirac Landau level on a Bravais lattice. The exact many-body wavefunctions are given, analytically, in terms of the matrix coordinate $X+iY+J$, where $(X,Y)$ are the lattice coordinates and $J$ is a nilpotent matrix in spin space. The constructed exact pairs cover the fractional Chern states of the Laughlin, the Read-Rezayi, and the Halperin series. Our results prove that FCI ground states exist beyond ideal bands.

items.title: Zero-Temperature Energetics of a First-Order Surface Phase Transition from Diffraction
items.summary: First-order phase transitions are governed by the balance between zero-temperature energy, thermal vibrational energy, and entropy, yet these contributions are rarely accessible experimentally. Here, we establish a diffraction-based route to determine them for the prototypical Si(111)-In atomic-wire system. From the temperature-dependent Debye-Waller attenuation of reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) intensities we extract distinct Debye temperatures for the low-temperature $(8{\times}2)$ ground state and the high-temperature $(4{\times}1)$ phase. The softer vibrational spectrum of the high-temperature phase yields the entropy gain that stabilizes this phase above the critical temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$. Evaluating the thermodynamic balance between internal energy and entropy at $T_\mathrm{c} = 125\,\mathrm{K}$ yields a zero-temperature energy difference of $ΔE_0 = 138\,\mathrm{meV}/(8{\times}2)$, including the difference in vibrational zero-point energies of the two phases, thus providing direct access to hidden thermodynamic parameters of a first-order surface phase transition.

items.title: A Nonsecular Quantum Master Equation with Detailed Balance and Second-order Error Bound
items.summary: An effective theory of open quantum systems should preserve the detailed balance structure inherited from microscopic reversibility and remain accurate throughout relaxation. Meeting both requirements is particularly challenging in quantum many-body systems, where dense spectra can invalidate the secular approximation even at weak coupling. Here we construct a nonsecular quantum master equation that satisfies time-reversal Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (TR-KMS) detailed balance. Under suitable conditions, we prove a time-uniform $O(λ^2)$ bound on the difference between the predicted and exact reduced density matrices, where $λ$ is the system-bath coupling strength. Our construction completes the Redfield generator by imposing detailed balance while matching its dissipative and coherent coefficients at resonance. In this approach, TR-KMS detailed balance is compatible with resonance matching, whereas its counterpart without time reversal is not. In a benchmark against the exact microscopic dynamics of two coupled oscillators, our equation maintains $O(λ^2)$ accuracy across secular and nonsecular regimes, outperforming the existing detailed-balance equations tested. These results provide a systematic route from microscopic models to thermodynamically consistent descriptions of open quantum dynamics beyond the secular approximation.

items.title: Prediction and Screening of $η$-carbide-type Nitrides for Ammonia Synthesis
items.summary: Synthesis of ammonia is of critical importance to applications in energy, industrial chemistry, and especially agriculture, and is accomplished industrially using the carbon- and energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process. η-carbide-type nitrides such as Co3Mo3N have gained attention in recent years as alternative ammonia synthesis catalysts with the potential to lower these energy demands. Co3Mo3N is experimentally observed to undergo a reversible phase transition from Co3Mo3N to Co6Mo6N, offering a chemical looping-based NH3 synthesis route that has not been fully explored. In this work, we present a first-principles exploration of phase change in the Co3Mo3N/Co6Mo6N system as a prototype η-carbide-type nitride and fit a cluster expansion to predict the energy of Co3Mo3Nx systems. We use our results to identify the phase energy difference as a useful screening criterion for the phase change process. We then apply this methodology to screen a broad range of η-carbide-type nitrides that combine group 4-6 transition metals with Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, or Zn. We report strong periodic trends in phase energy difference, which increases with decreasing period and group number of the group 4-6 transition metal and with distance from group 9 for the other metal. We identify Co3W3N, Fe3W3N, and several quaternary nitrides as promising candidates for NH3 synthesis via a phase change mechanism.

items.title: Finite-resolution exhaustive traversal of thermodynamic state spaces has divergent thermodynamic length
items.summary: Resolving a prescribed multidimensional control window by a single continuous, serial scan is a task distinct from driving between fixed endpoints. We formulate this task as metric coverage at resolution $\eps$. Classical covering estimates, applied to a compact regular $d$-dimensional Riemannian window, give a required length of order at least $\eps^{1-d}$; local grid traversals attain the same exponent. When a physical friction tensor uniformly dominates the coverage metric, this geometric cost implies a necessary duration of order at least $\eps^{-2(d-1)}$ at fixed quadratic excess-work budget. Fixed-duration divergence refers to the slow-driving quadratic action and is not a claim about exact work outside that regime. A detailed-balance three-state process and an overdamped harmonic trap provide microscopic friction examples. For the trap, independently integrated Gaussian moment dynamics approach the quadratic prediction as the prescribed raster is slowed, while refinement at a controlled work budget increases scan duration. A quasi-uniform operational resolution floor cuts off the geometric divergence. Landau-response and van der Waals proxy metrics serve separately as prescribed diagnostic geometries: independent quadrature tests their coordinate- and protocol-dependent critical prefactors without asserting universal critical dissipation. Morton ordering supplies an ordering/connector benchmark with larger finite-resolution amplitudes. The resulting resource statements apply to exhaustive serial coverage, with metric, interpolation and driving assumptions specified explicitly.

items.title: When Time-Reversible Sensor Records Require Hidden Dissipation
items.summary: A binary sensor record can be time reversible yet require dissipation in every compatible finite-state Markov model. For a four-state sensor with correlated dwell times, two observed switching statistics give an exact equilibrium criterion and, when equilibrium is excluded, a positive lower bound on entropy production independent of hidden-state number. An explicit four-state construction provides an upper bound on the minimum dissipation. For a noisy Poisson sensor, the bounds differ by less than a factor of two and vanish at a kinetic matching point while the sensor remains dissipative.

items.title: A Liquid Film Can Survive without Being Bulk-Like: Rupture and Mechanical Isotropy Set Different Thickness Limits in Lennard-Jones Films
items.summary: How thick must a liquid film be before its middle behaves like ordinary bulk liquid? Free-standing films are the standard geometry for computing surface properties by molecular simulation and the simplest model of soap and foam films, coatings and polymer layers, yet the question is seldom answered quantitatively. We answer it for Lennard-Jones films by comparing two criteria: whether the film survives without rupturing, and whether the lateral pressure at its center has relaxed to the bulk value. Covering three interaction ranges (cutoffs rc = 3.5-7.5 times sigma), three temperatures and lateral system sizes from 20 to 100 times sigma, we find that the two criteria give different thicknesses and respond to different parameters. Films thinner than 6-7 times sigma (about 2 nm for argon) rupture within 105 tau (~0.2 microseconds); this kinetic limit hardly depends on the interaction range but grows with the lateral size of the system, and close to it rupture is an activated event. The center becomes mechanically bulk-like only at a larger thickness h*, where the tangential anisotropy computed with the Irving-Kirkwood definition falls below 0.003 epsilon x sigma^3; h* grows from ~11 times sigma (3.8 nm) to ~15 times sigma (5 nm) as the cutoff increases from 3.5 to 7.5 times sigma, but it is nearly independent of temperature and of lateral size. Between the two limits films are long-lived yet perturbed throughout. Neither the surface tension, which shows no thickness dependence, nor the central density, whose relative deficit is about 16 times smaller than the relative anisotropy, reveals this perturbation: the stress detects confinement before the structure does.

items.title: From geometric curvature to effective backgrounds: a dictionary for Dirac fermions in one, two and three spatial dimensions
items.summary: Dirac equation on curved backgrounds can be rewritten as a flat-space equation in which geometry appears as a tensorial Fermi velocity together with a set of background fields. We derive this correspondence from a single Clifford-algebra identity and follow it through one, two, and three spatial dimensions. Once the spin connection is written in terms of Ricci rotation coefficients, only two contractions can occur. The trace produces a term with the index structure of a vector potential in every dimensionality; it enters with an imaginary factor i and is precisely the term that keeps the operator Hermitian when the Fermi velocity depends on position. The totally antisymmetric contraction produces an object that depends on the number of indices available to the Levi-Civita symbol: a trace on a line, a pseudoscalar mass on a surface, and an axial vector potential in a volume. Neither contraction is invariant under local rotations of the frame, and we give the transformation laws. On a surface, the curl of the trace term can always be removed by a frame rotation, while its divergence is proportional to the Gaussian curvature. We apply the correspondence to a Gaussian bump, where the local density of states at the center falls below its flat value and obeys a closed form at low energy; to a wire, where a nonuniform lapse binds states inside the gap and a nonuniform velocity cannot; to stationary frames on a surface, where a circulating drag shifts the Dirac mass locally with either sign; and to twisted and rotating frames in a volume, where the axial term takes the form of a chiral chemical potential produced by the frame alone, or separates Weyl nodes in a rotating sample. We separate the geometric contribution from the lattice pseudogauge field that dominates the response of strained samples

items.title: Models and Measures of Statistical Physics and Sociophysics for Fracture Mechanics and Earthquake Dynamics: An Introduction
items.summary: The breaking or fracture of materials and damages or devastations due to earthquakes have caught our attention since the earliest stage of human civilization. In fact, at around 1500, Leonardo da Vinci made the pioneering observation that, unlike elastic constants (formalized later by Hooke in 1678) of the materials, the tensile (breaking) strengths of nominally identical iron wires decrease drastically with increasing their length, indicating the vanishing breaking strength of materials in the large-size limit, suggesting the impossibility of constructing arbitrarily large structures. This was the first observation that, unlike the elasticity of disordered materials, which remains defined in the thermodynamic limit (self-averaging statistics), the breaking properties of the disordered materials have extreme (non-self-averaging) statistics. In spite of major and some precise developments in statistical physical modelling and characterizing the fracture mechanics (starting with Alan Griffith's crack nucleation theory in 1921 and the weakest link failure Fibre Bundle Model of Frederick Thomas Peirce in 1926) and of earthquake dynamics (starting with Robert Burridge and Leon Knopoff's continuum dynamical model in 1967 and later other discrete or lattice train models or fractal overlap models of stick-slip earthquakes), no graduate-level textbook in condensed matter physics or in statistical physics introduces the basic models and their properties. And now computer scientists and social scientists (coming with their social inequality measures applied to the avalanche statistics in precursor failures) are joining their efforts to explore the new precursory inequality measures for big avalanches or failures. This introductory review is designed to fill this gap with a view to introducing these to this wider audience and to take them to the current frontiers in these fields.

items.title: Geometric limits of quantum recovery across an Ising transition
items.summary: How many physical spins must a receiver retain to recover an unknown qubit? Four Ising duality defects encode a qubit over a common pure bulk ground state in a fixed charge sector. We vary that state at fixed defect geometry and optimize over preselected spins and joint decoders, taking the infinite-chain limit before increasing defect separation. At every fixed finite positive reference field, exact recovery costs the central spacing plus the shorter outer spacing to leading order. For an error falling as any fixed inverse power of separation, the leading cost is the central spacing in the ordered phase, the shorter outer spacing in the disordered phase and their sum at criticality. Order and disorder records in discarded spins explain the contrast. In a critical benchmark, single-spin measurements, a one-way classical message and an output correction preserve reference entanglement on two separated blocks at budgets where every connected interval is entanglement breaking.

items.title: 4D-TEMPO: Differentiable 4D-STEM ptychography via fast Physics Optimizers
items.summary: Electron ptychography recovers atomic structure from 4D-STEM data: diffraction patterns at multiple positions of a scanned probe. Current codes reconstruct an image and read atoms off it, or fit atoms under an $L_1$ loss; neither gives per-atom uncertainty. We propose 4D-TEMPO, a differentiable physical renderer that fits the atoms, the microscope, and the detector directly to the recorded electron counts under a Poisson likelihood. The output is a list of atoms, each a Gaussian primitive with a 3D position, a thermal width, and a model-conditional error bar from the Fisher information. The Fisher information also conditions the solver, gives the dose (electrons per Å$^2$) each parameter needs, and separates calibration from imaging. On a simulated WSe$_2$ bilayer, starting from the published reconstruction, fitted atoms cut in-plane error by a third (3.2 vs. 4.8 pm) and depth error by 40-61% against its 3D peaks. Depth comes from multiple scattering into the dark field, the faint counts outside the direct beam. The two layers, $10\times$ closer than the depth of field, separate; per-atom depth then follows the layer geometry. When the model is well specified, the bars are calibrated (69% of position coordinates within $1σ$). On experimental WSe$_2$, fitted atoms predict held-out patterns better than the three published codes we test. With free probe modes where atoms are incomplete, the same likelihood predicts best on all three held-out benchmarks, matches every WSe$_2$ baseline in 5 min against up to 20.5 h, and passes torchslice at its released setting 180$\times$ sooner on PrScO$_3$. Per-atom error bars, planned doses, and fast reconstruction point to low-dose, real-time 3D imaging of beam-sensitive and dynamic materials.
