items.title: Issue Publication Information
Issue Editorial Masthead
Non-Hermitian skin effect and quasiperiodicity-induced localization in a photonic lattice with staggered on-site potentials
authors: Jia-Yi Li, Zhi-Xu Zhang, Jie Zhang, Kai-Xin Hu, Wen-Xue Cui, Ji Cao and Hong-Fu Wang
items.summary: The quasicrystals combined with nonreciprocal and on-site non-Hermiticity provide a unique platform to explore exceptional phenomena arising from the non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE). Especially, we investigate a non-Hermitian photonic lattice with nonreciprocal hoppings and staggered complex on-site potentials, revealing an energy-dependent bipolar NHSE and a quasiperiodicity-driven redistribution from skin states to bulk-localized states. Numerical winding numbers and analytical contact conditions reveal the spectral reconnections underlying the bipolar NHSE, with the sign of the imaginary eigenenergy determining its localization direction. Meanwhile, imaginary quasiperiodic modulation drives a crossover from skin localization to bulk localization, while real and imaginary modulations yield comparable bulk localization at strong modulation. Moreover, Fibonacci-size calculations support persistent skin–bulk coexistence, while a separable two-dimensional extension connects one-dimensional localization directions to corner accumulation and spatial redistribution. These results provide a unified framework for understanding and controlling the interplay between spectral topology and quasiperiodicity in non-Hermitian photonic systems.

items.title: Enhancing soil carbon to address the joint climate and biodiversity crises
High-rate and durable sodium-ion batteries enabled by charge-asymmetric single-atom-energized hard carbon
items.summary: Abstract Sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) represent a promising complement to lithium-based systems due to the abundant supply and cost-effectiveness of sodium. However, the widespread adoption of SIBs is practically hindered by the lack of cycling-stable hard-carbon anodes with superior capacity and rate capability. Here, we show a design of high-rate and durable SIB anodes achieved by introducing main-group metal single atoms ( M SA = Sb, Bi, Sn) featuring a unique charge-asymmetric N 4 – M SA –O 2 moiety anchored on nitrogen-doped hard carbon ( M SA @NC). This designed charge-asymmetric configuration establishes a dynamically evolving atomic interface that adaptively modulates active sites to achieve significant improvements in both Na + storage kinetics and capacity. The representative Sb SA @NC system demonstrates high specific capacity, improved rate capability and cyclability in both coin and pouch-type cells. Extensive experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the structural rearrangement of the N 4 –Sb–O 2 moiety during (de)sodiation is highly reversible and energetically favorable, enabling enhanced reversible capacity (422.8 mAh g −1 at 0.1 A g −1 ) and rate capability (207.6 mAh g −1 at 20 A g −1 ) while preserving material integrity. This work offers a promising pathway in advancing high-performing HC anodes for fast-charging and durable SIBs.

items.title: Single-atom catalyst–Li2O2 interfacial chemistry governs the activity–stability trade-off in Li–O2 batteries
items.summary: Abstract Cathode catalysts in aprotic Li–O 2 batteries are commonly judged by their ability to lower charge overpotentials, yet improved catalytic activity often does not lead to durable cycling. Here, we use structurally well-defined M–N 4 single-atom catalysts (SACs) as model cathodes to elucidate the interplay between catalyst activity and battery stability. Integrated experimental and theoretical studies suggest that, although SACs promote Li 2 O 2 oxidation and lower the initial charging overpotential, they also increase the reactivity of discharge-generated Li 2 O 2 toward ether electrolytes, promoting carboxylate accumulation and cathode passivation. On the basis of this mechanistic insight, a localized high-concentration electrolyte is introduced to regulate the catalyst–Li 2 O 2 interfacial chemistry, suppress side reactions, and extend the cycling life from 42 to 398 cycles. This work identifies a previously overlooked trade-off between catalytic activity and battery stability in Li–O 2 batteries and provides a mechanistic foundation for designing stable catalyst/electrolyte interfaces in high-energy electrochemical devices.

items.title: Thermal-fluctuator-driven decoherence of an oscillator near-resonantly coupled to a two-level system
authors: Thomas J Antolin, Jonas Glatthard and Andrew D Armour
items.summary: Recent experiments on a range of engineered quantum systems have highlighted the important role of interacting two-level systems (TLSs) in modifying device properties and generating fluctuations. Focusing on the case of an oscillator coupled to a single near-resonant TLS, we explore how interactions between the TLS and lower-frequency thermally activated two-level fluctuators (TLFs) degrade the oscillator’s coherence. Depending on the strength of the couplings, a single TLF can give rise to coherence oscillations that appear alongside, or supplant, Rabi oscillations of the oscillator–TLS system. Bath-driven transitions in the TLF cause irreversible coherence decay at a rate that is highly sensitive to both the couplings and the transition rate. For an ensemble of TLFs, we identify and characterise the different regimes of non-exponential phase-averaging-driven coherence decay that the oscillator can display. Using numerical calculations, we examine the extent to which systems with just a few TLFs differ from the limit of a large (continuum) TLF ensemble. Our work provides a theoretical framework for understanding the interplay of coherent TLS interactions and TLF-induced dephasing in quantum devices such as superconducting and phononic resonators.

items.title: Sensitive Thermometry with a Fiber-Integrated Optical Microcavity
authors: Min She, 敏 佘, Qiang Zhang, 强 张, Zhao An, 钊 安, Fan Lv, 帆 吕, Zhaoyi Liu, 兆亿 刘, Jitao Cao, 济韬 曹, Yuhong Zou, 榆红 邹, Ruikai Pan, 瑞恺 潘, Wenpeng Zhou, 文鹏 周, Han Zhang, 涵 张, Jiangshan Tang, 江山 唐, Feng Wang, 峰 王, Franco Nori, Keyu Xia and 可宇 夏
items.summary: High-sensitivity thermometry is critical for cutting-edge technologies such as gravimeters, quantum clocks, and lithography systems. Although recent transformative advances in resonator-based optical microthermometers achieve high sensitivity, the input and output setups are complex and require precise control, severely limiting their practical applications and achievable footprint. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a fiber-integrated thermometer made of a high-Q optical Fabry–Pérot fiber microcavity, filled with transparent but thermal-sensitive ultraviolet glue. The input and transmitted probe laser fields are coupled to the microthermometer via optical fibers, significantly facilitating operation and minimizing the device size. Combining the large temperature dependence of the ultraviolet glue and the micrometer-scale cavity, sensitive thermometry is achieved by independently measuring the resonance shift or the transmission change. Based on evaluation of equivalent temperature noise of the power spectral density, the resonance-shift method achieves microkelvin-level sensitivity. The fixed-wavelength transmission-change method yields a nanokelvin-level readout-referred equivalent temperature-noise floor at high frequencies using quasi-static response calibration. This low-cost, simple, and fiber-integrated microthermometer holds significant potential for applications in quantum device characterization, biocalorimetry, optoelectronic technologies, and next-generation clocks.

items.title: Double Cavity Exceptional-Point Enhanced Laser Cooling of Semiconductors
authors: Haonan Chang, 浩男 常, Feilong Song, 飞龙 宋, Jun Zhang and 俊 张
items.summary: Laser cooling of semiconductors requires a high external quantum efficiency for phonon-assisted upconversion while suppressing heat generated by background absorption and non-radiative relaxation. Nanophotonic resonances can strengthen the upconversion channel, but in a single-mode structure may also enhance parasitic pump heating. We introduce a two-cavity non-Hermitian architecture that separates preparation of a lower reservoir state from extraction of the phonon-promoted radiative state. A passive exceptional point, containing no optical gain, is placed in the output branch, where it reshapes the projected final-state optical response; all anti-Hermitian diagonal terms describe radiative leakage, internal absorption, or material decay. For a CdS parameter set, the four-mode calculation gives a 1.23 × 103 enhancement of upconverted photoluminescence relative to a single-mode control, while the pump-induced heat load rises by only 2.8 × 10–3%. The gain consists of a factor of 3.45 × 102 from the independent output resonance and a further factor of 3.56 from exceptional-point tuning.

items.title: Interference-Controlled Nonclassical Photon Emission via Cavity-Mediated Spin Exchange
items.summary: The generation of nonclassical light with strong photon antibunching and appreciable brightness remains an important goal in quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate that cavity-mediated spin-exchange interactions provide a route to overcome this constraint by amplifying spectral anharmonicity. In a two-emitter cavity-QED system with a controllable relative phase ϕ, the resulting interference–interaction mechanism reshapes the dressed-state manifold and enables switching between distinct quantum emission regimes. For ϕ = 0, constructive interference yields high-quality single-photon emission with near-perfect antibunching, suppressing by more than three orders of magnitude while maintaining a substantial intracavity photon population. Conversely, for ϕ =π, destructive interference suppresses direct single-photon excitation and selectively enhances two-photon excitation, producing signatures of correlated two-photon emission with appreciable intracavity photon populations and suppressed higher-order excitations. Our work establishes interference-engineered interactions as a mechanism for the controllable selection of single-photon and photon-pair emission, opening new opportunities for programmable nonclassical light sources and quantum photonic applications.

items.title: Pulse-Controlled Topologically Protected Quantum Batteries
authors: Jin Yang, 瑾 杨, Biao Xiong, 标 熊, Jibing Liu, 继兵 刘, Houguo Yu, 厚果 余, Dehua Liu, 德华 刘, Feng Mei, 锋 梅, Chuanjia Shan and 传家 单
items.summary: Remote charging in the field of quantum batteries is particularly appealing because it minimizes interference between the charger and the battery, making it a subject of considerable interest. Here, we propose a robust remote charging protocol for quantum batteries based on a pulse-controlled superconducting qubit chain. By dynamically modulating the pulse-mediated couplings, we realize chiral-symmetry-protected energy transfer from the charger to the battery. We show that the charging process suppresses energy backflow due to the pulse control and remains robust against pulse imperfections due to the chiral symmetry of the system. Moreover, the energy stored in the battery at the target time is almost fully extractable, and the protocol remains effective over a moderate range of chain lengths. To further accelerate charging, we optimize the pulse shape and elucidate the underlying physical mechanism. Our pulse-controlled topological quantum battery protocol provides a versatile framework for implementing remote topological charging and establishes a theoretical foundation for designing optimal-control strategies to enhance quantum battery performance.

items.title: Switchable Auxetic Piezoelectricity in Rhombohedral Relaxor Ferroelectrics
authors: He-Meng Sun, 和猛 孙, Hang-Bo Zhang, 杭波 张, Zhi Tan, 智 谭, Ming-Min Yang and 明敏 杨
items.summary: Piezoelectric materials typically exhibit opposite longitudinal and transverse mechanical responses under an electric field, reflecting the electromechanical analogue of a positive Poisson’s ratio. Auxetic piezoelectricity, in which longitudinal and transverse coefficients share the same sign, has recently emerged as an unconventional electromechanical response; yet its intrinsic realization and electrical tunability in relaxor ferroelectrics with complex domain structures remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate intrinsic and electrically switchable auxetic piezoelectricity in rhombohedral relaxor ferroelectric Pb(Mg1/3Nb2/3)O3-PbTiO3 by combining first-principles calculations and quantitative piezoelectric measurements. Density functional perturbation theory reveals that a positive transverse piezoelectric response is symmetry-allowed in the rhombohedral phase and primarily originates from internal-strain contributions associated with cooperative Pb-O displacements. Experiments on single-domain (111)pc-oriented crystals confirm the existence of an intrinsic auxetic state. Beyond the single-domain limit, in situ bias-dependent measurements reveal continuous and reversible electric-field-driven switching between auxetic and conventional piezoelectric states within the same crystal. A tensor-rotation-based multi-domain model quantitatively reproduces the bias-dependent response and identifies domain redistribution, enabled by the large shear piezoelectric coefficient, as the microscopic origin of the switching behavior. These findings establish auxetic piezoelectricity as an intrinsic and electrically programmable response in rhombohedral relaxor ferroelectrics, providing a general route toward reconfigurable electromechanical functionalities.

items.title: Beyond Classical Nucleation: Density-Controlled Relaxation Mechanism in Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
authors: Yue Shan, 月 单, Pengfei Zhang, 朋飞 张, Chun-Lai Ren, 春来 任, Yu-Qiang Ma and 余强 马
items.summary: A recent experiment [Natl. Sci. Rev. 13 nwag107 (2026)] revealed a density transition during nucleation of intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), yet its physical origin remains unresolved. Here, using minimal coarse-grained sticker–spacer models, we identify a density-controlled relaxation mechanism governing nucleation under weak multivalent interactions. This mechanism emerges across three hierarchical levels. At the cluster level, nucleation proceeds via reversible, density-regulated nuclei beyond classical nucleation theory. At the molecular level, the configurational distributions of chains within nucleating clusters evolve non-monotonically with cluster size relative to those of isolated single chains, while their conformational fluctuations exhibit exponential relaxation with a characteristic timescale ( ). At the bond level, reversible bond turnover accelerates with cluster growth, yielding a characteristic aggregation number (N *) that marks density saturation and the onset of irreversible growth. The correspondence between and N * reveals that nucleation is intrinsically governed by relaxation dynamics. These results establish density-controlled bond turnover as a key kinetic regulator of IDP nucleation and provide a general framework for phase transitions driven by weak multivalent interactions.

Integrated photonic technologies also provide a clear path for scaling trapped-ion quantum computing architectures. This work presents an integrated photonic optical clock as a complete system, confining up to four Yb ions at separate sites at room temperature. By autonomously identifying lost ions, loading new ones, and shuttling the replacements, even when individual ions are lost the system maintains continuous clock operation uninterrupted for more than two hours.

items.title: Efficient quantum Gibbs sampling of stabilizer codes using hybrid computation
authors: Ivan H C Shum and Angela Capel
items.summary: We present hybrid Gibbs sampling algorithms for the stabilizer code Hamiltonians of the rotated surface code and the toric code with only local quantum algorithms, using quantum circuit depth to prepare the Gibbs state of the rotated surface code Hamiltonian, and quantum circuit depth to prepare the Gibbs state of the toric code Hamiltonian, being the side of the side of the square lattice. We further show that if we allow for non-local gates, the Gibbs state of the periodic 1D Ising model can be prepared in logarithmic depth and linearly many simultaneous measurements.

items.title: An active Lorentz gas: walking droplets in periodic media
authors: Aleksi Majaniemi, Esko Toivonen, Rahil N Valani, Rainer Klages and Esa Räsänen
items.summary: The Lorentz gas is a paradigmatic model in dynamical systems theory for understanding the origin of nonequilibrium transport in terms of microscopic deterministic chaos. In the periodic setting, a point particle scatters elastically off disks arranged on a two-dimensional lattice. Here we replace the disks by smooth potentials and the particle by the widely studied walking droplet, which propels itself on a vertically vibrating fluid. In the low-memory limit, this droplet reduces to a particle with nonlinear active friction. We call this system an active Lorentz gas. Using extensive numerical simulations, we analyse how dissipation generated by the active deterministic dynamics alters the phase-space structure of the corresponding conservative Lorentz gas. We find that islands of stability collapse into attracting and repelling sets. To characterize these structures, we introduce an energy-variance filtering method that distinguishes localized periodic, quasi-ballistic periodic, and chaotic trajectories, enabling the construction of bifurcation diagrams in a non-conservative setting. We identify parameter regimes exhibiting strong bifurcation cascades, anomalous diffusion, and significant phase-space contraction. Our results establish the active Lorentz gas as a rich framework for studying transport in dissipative dynamical systems and provide a bridge between active matter and classical models of chaotic transport, with potential implications for hydrodynamic quantum analogs in periodic media.

items.title: Generative diffusion model with inverse renormalization group flows
items.summary: Natural data contain structure across multiple length scales, yet exploiting these correlations for efficient generation remains challenging. Applications to protein structure prediction and image generation demonstrate improved sample quality or sampling speed over denoising diffusion probabilistic model baselines with the same network architectures, highlighting how physical principles can guide the design of efficient generative models.

items.summary: Non-Abelian gauge fields provide a powerful framework for exploring exotic topological states, yet their interplay with space-time symmetries remains largely unexplored. Cao et al. introduce the concept of non-Abelian space-time lattice gauge fields and experimentally realize them using space-time topolectrical circuits, revealing geometry-dependent higher-order topological states and unconventional topological phase transitions with indirect band crossings. This opens avenues for exploring non-Abelian topological physics beyond the limitations of static systems.

items.summary: Density scaling successfully describes how temperature and packing jointly control molecular motion in equilibrium liquids, but whether it applies to glasses has remained open. Stavropoulou et al. simultaneously track molecular relaxation and densification during physical aging of a molecular glass and show that the two evolve in strict proportionality. The proportionality factor is predicted, without adjustable parameters, from equilibrium density scaling parameters, extending this framework to the nonequilibrium glassy state.

items.title: Coupled propagation of acoustic topological states
authors: Ming-Zhu Li, Lei Shi, Zhe-Yu Ji, Zhaojiang Chen and Ya-Xi Shen
items.summary: We theoretically and experimentally investigate the coupled propagation of two pseudospin states in an acoustic topological heterostructure. Within the framework of coupled-mode theory, the heterostructure is mapped onto a two-waveguide model, in which the two pseudospin topological states serve as guiding modes. The propagation constants of the individual topological states and the coupling strength between them are quantitatively extracted from the projected band structures of supercells. When the two topological states are decoupled, acoustic energy remains confined to the excited topological interface. When the two topological states are coupled, acoustic energy undergoes Bloch oscillation between two topological interfaces. Notably, the energy-transfer coefficient of the Bloch oscillation can be tuned by introducing interface detuning. Owing to the frequency dispersion of the coupling strength, the heterostructure can function as a wavelength-selective demultiplexer. This work establishes a generalized coupled-mode framework for the quantitative analysis and flexible manipulation of topological-state coupling, offering new insights into the design of topologically protected acoustic devices with controllable multichannel functionalities.

items.title: 2D quantum-path interference in high-harmonic generation driven by highly-bichromatic fields
authors: Xiaozhou Zou, Lucie Jurkovičová, Anne Weber, Cong Zhao, Martin Albrecht, Ondřej Finke, Alexandr Vendl, Annika Grenfell, Wojciech Szuba, Jaroslav Nejdl, Eric Constant, Margarita Khokhlova, Emilio Pisanty, Ondřej Hort and Amelle Zaïr
items.summary: We experimentally observe a new type of quantum-path interference, in two-dimensions (2D-QPI), in high-harmonic generation (HHG) driven by an orthogonally-polarised highly-bichromatic field. This regime is characterised by a relatively strong orthogonal second-harmonic component beyond the weak perturbation limit, such that the electron dynamics are substantially modified. In this highly-bichromatic regime, we demonstrate that 2D-QPI is encoded in the measured harmonic intensity modulations with respect to the relative phase of the two-colour field. The modulations of the odd-order harmonics show a monomodal behaviour, whereas the even harmonics are modulated in a bimodal structure. Our calculations using the strong-field approximation and saddle-point method disentangle contributions from multiple quantum orbits in this HHG regime, revealing that the dipole response for both odd and even harmonics inherits the dynamic symmetry of the orthogonally-polarised driving field. This new type of 2D-QPI offers a novel route to HHG spectroscopy of attosecond electron dynamics by lifting up the dimensionality of the quantum paths involved in the interference.

items.title: Magnon-mediated cooling by heating in a spin-selective quantum dot system
items.summary: We demonstrate how nonequilibrium magnons can drive the cooling by heating effect in a spin-selective quantum dot system. The mechanism relies on magnon-assisted spin-flip transitions that transfer electrons between two ferromagnetic electrodes maintained at different temperatures, with the magnetic insulator acting as the high-temperature energy source. In the limit of fully spin-polarized antiparallel electrodes, the transport enters a tight-coupling regime in which each absorbed magnon is accompanied by the transfer of a single electron. This one-to-one correspondence directly links the cooling power to the heat supplied by the magnonic reservoir and enables the thermodynamic performance to approach its upper bound. We further show how finite spin polarization introduces parasitic spin channels that suppress cooling and reduce the operating range. An extended dual quantum dot configuration restores cooling by heating without net charge current and enhances the cooling power. Our results establish magnons as a distinct microscopic energy carrier for cooling by heating and provide a route toward its realization in solid-state spin-caloritronic systems.

items.summary: Yang–Mills (YM) theory has evolved beyond its origins in the strong interaction to become an effective framework for condensed matter, ultracold atomic, and photonic systems, where synthetic non-Abelian gauge fields enable phenomena such as spin transport, the spin-Hall effect, and polarization control. These systems provide access to gauge-field dynamics beyond the reach of high-energy experiments. In all the above mentioned cases, the state of the system evolves in an effective external YM field. Here, we report the results of a classical study (as preparatory for a full quantum study) of particle dynamics in constant gauge fields produced by constant gauge potentials, by focusing on configurations that are experimentally relevant. We show that consequences such as unbounded trajectories in a constant color magnetic field and unusual correlation between charge and color dynamics have a direct bearing on the physical phenomena observed, especially in experiments involving charge and spin transports. More generally, this work also shows how the low energy systems can act as laboratories to probe quintessentially non-Abelian features such as the Wu-Yang ambiguity.

items.title: The Answer Lies within the Puzzle Piece: PET-Derived Defect-rich MOFs Boosting Ethylene Glycol Oxidation for Total-Product PET Upcycling
authors: Jiaqi Zhang, Tingting Chen, Zhicheng Tan, Chengjin Chen, Chen’an Zhou, Junliang Chen, Jianping Yang, and Zhongjie Huang
items.summary: Abstract Chemical recycling of poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) is limited by harsh depolymerization conditions and the low-value utilization of terephthalic acid (TPA) and ethylene glycol (EG). Herein, we report a “one-stone-three-birds” strategy that couples PET depolymerization, TPA utilization, and EG upgrading for total-product upcycling. Waste PET serves as an in situ slow-release terephthalate precursor, whose gradual, incomplete hydrolysis dynamically perturbs metal–ligand stoichiometry, generating missing-linker defects and oxygen-deficient, coordinatively unsaturated environments in a bimetallic MOF (NiCo-PET). Relative to NiCo-MOF prepared from commercial TPA, NiCo-PET exhibits 67% higher spin concentration and enhanced EG oxidation, requiring only 1.29 V vs RHE at 50 mA cm –2 while achieving 93.6% formate Faradaic efficiency and stable operation for 24 h at 2 A cm –2 . Operando analysis confirms favorable reconstruction into high-valence oxyhydroxides. This work valorizes both PET-derived products without additional purification or isolation, offering a sustainable route to total-product plastic upcycling.

items.title: Operando Imaging of Battery Interfaces through Combined Analysis of Broadband Optical Backgrounds and Raman Features
authors: Shengfu Wei, Zhengcheng Gu, Yufeng Zhang, Weigang Ma, Aoran Fan, and Xing Zhang
items.summary: Abstract Solid-state batteries promise improved safety and energy density, but their performance is governed by buried interfaces where ion transport, chemical reactions, and stress evolution are strongly coupled. Resolving these processes during operation remains challenging. Here, we present an operando spectroscopic strategy that jointly analyzes broadband optical backgrounds and characteristic electrolyte Raman features within a single measurement. Asymmetric least-squares baseline (ALS) estimation extracts broadband optical contrast associated with lithium distribution, while Raman band intensities and peak positions provide complementary information on interfacial chemistry and local stress estimates. This capability provides a unified optical framework for visualizing structural, chemical, and mechanical evolution at battery interfaces and offers a broadly applicable route to interrogate buried interphases in diverse electrochemical systems. More generally, by enabling real-time, multimodal insight into interfacial dynamics, this method advances efforts toward safer, longer-lasting, and more predictable energy-storage technologies.

items.title: Resolving Overlapping Signals in Quantum Relaxometry Enabled by Spectral Hole Burning
authors: Fei Kong, Zhehua Huang, Zhengze Zhao, Pengju Zhao, Zhecheng Wang, Ya Wang, and Fazhan Shi
items.summary: Abstract Quantum relaxometry based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond is an easy-to-use technique that detects magnetic noise by measuring the longitudinal relaxation of NV centers. It is favored in chemical and biological applications due to the robustness against imperfect spin control. By tuning the energy level, NV relaxometry can detect magnetic noise generated by other spins and obtain magnetic resonance spectra through cross relaxation. However, the spectral resolution is greatly limited by the inhomogeneous broadening of NV centers, especially for nanodiamond-based relaxometry. Here we demonstrate a hole-burning technique to remove the inhomogeneous broadening. We utilize a weak pump field to deplete specific NV centers during the relaxation measurement, which contribute a reverse signal in the cross-relaxation spectra with a much narrower line width. Our method retains the convenience and sensitivity of NV relaxometry, opening up new avenues for high-resolution magnetic resonance spectroscopy in complex scenarios.

items.title: Reversible Electric-Field-Induced Changes in the Thermal Resistance of Hexagonal Boron Nitride
authors: Amelia Schaeffer, Lena Fine, Aloyse Maille, Thomas Poirier, Joyce Christiansen-Salameh, Gustavo Alvarez, James H. Edgar, and Zhiting Tian
items.summary: Abstract Understanding the behavior of ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) materials under high electric fields is essential for advancing next-generation power electronics. While electrical degradation processes have been widely studied, the influence of high electric fields on thermal transport remains largely unexplored. Here, we report the first experimental measurements of changing thermal resistance under an applied electric field in a UWBG material, using single-crystalline hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) as a model system. We observe substantial, and sometimes reversible, changes in thermal resistance during prolonged exposure to a strong DC electric field. These results reveal a previously unrecognized sensitivity of phonon transport to high-field electrical stressing and show that thermal resistance can serve as a sensitive probe of electric-field-induced material evolution that remains undetected by conventional electrical characterization. More broadly, this work establishes thermal transport measurements as a powerful tool for investigating high-field phenomena in UWBG materials.

items.title: Atomically Precise Au 14 V 1 Clusters Selectively Block the Neutrophil Elastase-NETosis Axis
authors: Sufei Zhou, Yili Wang, Guo Li, Hongli Yu, Chenxi Li, Si Sun, Qi Xin, Nan Song, Di Liu, Xiao-Dong Zhang, and Hao Wang
items.summary: Abstract Neutrophil elastase (NE) is a key driver of neutrophil-mediated inflammation and tissue injury across diverse diseases. However, current NE inhibitors often lack sufficient target selectivity, limiting their therapeutic efficacy in suppressing inflammation and promoting organ repair. Here, we report that single-atom V doping programs atomically precise Au 15 clusters into a relatively selective and potent NE inhibitor. The ultrasmall size of Au 14 V 1 enables selective accommodation within the NE binding pocket. Multiscale mechanistic analyses demonstrated that Au 14 V 1 inhibits NE through a reversible mixed inhibition mechanism with an inhibition rate of 87.6%, while exhibiting minimal activity toward closely related proteases, highlighting its preferential inhibition toward NE. In LPS- and CLP-induced systemic inflammatory injury models, Au 14 V 1 reduced NE activity and NET formation, alleviated oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, mitigated tissue injury, and improved survival. These findings establish a single-atom engineering strategy for developing selective enzyme modulators and precise therapy targeting the NE-NETosis axis.

items.title: Single-Reactor-Run Architecture of Cleaving Homoepitaxial GaN with Aperture-Driven Disordered BN Interlayers
authors: Jungyong Shin, Bohyeon Kim, Anh Thi Dieu Nguyen, Nimphy Sarkar, Asif Ullah, Minhyeok Shin, Taenam Kwon, Sanghoon Kim, Seon Namgung, and Kunook Chung
items.summary: Abstract High-quality freestanding GaN membranes are fabricated using a single-reactor-run metal–organic chemical vapor deposition. The procedure begins with the growth of a single-crystalline GaN template, followed by the formation of a 20 nm-thick full-coverage disordered BN layer on GaN, which remains stable under high-temperature GaN growth conditions. We introduce a heat-treatment step to generate numerous nanoscale apertures in the BN layer, enabling aperture-mediated homoepitaxial regrowth. Meanwhile, the BN layer suppresses strong epitaxial bonding, where the regrown GaN is mechanically detachable from the GaN template. In addition, multiple disordered BN interlayer formations are established, enabling epitaxial lateral overgrowth (ELOG). Moreover, GaN Schottky diodes are fabricated to demonstrate minimal material degradation through the aperture-mediated lift-off process, enhanced device performance with BN-assisted ELOG, and the feasibility of ultralight wearable UV detectors. This approach eliminates the need for ex situ transfer or substrate-specific lift-off processes, providing a simple and thermally robust platform for manufacturing freestanding wide-bandgap semiconductor membranes.
